name: Learning-Space Coefficient Spaces Are Euclidean
statement: For every learning space $L$, logarithmic coefficient ratios identify $\mathcal A(L)$ with a nonempty open convex domain $\mathcal D_L\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_L}$, and $\mathcal A(L)\cong\mathbb R^{d_L}$.
proof: Writing root-witness magnitudes as exponentials makes every feasibility inequality a strict log-sum-exp inequality jointly convex in row logs and witness logs. Projection gives an open convex coefficient domain. A Minkowski-functional radial map identifies any nonempty open convex domain with Euclidean space.
